H01.text: Oh! Hello! You're new! Welcome to Letter Town! I'm Hudson, your community ambassador, and I'm very glad you're here.

H02.text: Around here, flowers grow letters, letters make words, and words can become wonderful things.

H03.text: What should we call you? You can choose a name for your town book.

H04.text: Wonderful! It's a pleasure to meet you. Let's get you acquainted with the town.

H05.text: You can take each lesson when you're ready. You can always return to me, and you can repeat a lesson whenever you like.

H06.text: First, our deputy mayor, Snowy, would love to show you your town book and map.

H07.text: Ready for our next stop? Or would you like more time here? There's no rush.

S01.text: Welcome. I'm Snowy, deputy mayor. I help keep the town records and make sure nobody gets lost. Usually.

S02.text: This is your town book. It keeps your map, useful information, and the important things you've learned.

S03.text: Try turning a page. You may use the page controls or the quick tabs, whichever is more comfortable.

S04.text: Now choose the map tab. The map will help you find the places you're welcome to visit.

S05.text: You'll find the garden, shops, town square, and the mayor's office here. More places will become available as the town grows.

S06.text: You can close or minimize the book without losing your place. Open it again whenever you need it.

S07.text: Would you like to practice page turns and tabs again? That's what practice is for.

S08.text: Excellent. I've marked the lesson complete. You can review these instructions in your book later.

S09.text: Return to Hudson whenever you're ready. He'll be waiting.

H08.text: Next up is Merry's Green Room! She'll show you how to grow a letter flower, water it, and pick it.

H09.text: Everything in practice stays in practice. You won't spend your real coins or use up your own seeds here.

M01.text: Hello, new friend! I'm Merry. Welcome to the Green Room! Every wonderful word begins somewhere.

M02.text: Let's start with a seed. Choose one, then pick an empty garden plot.

M03.text: There we go! A tiny beginning! Now we'll help it grow.

M04.text: Take the watering can and give the plant a drink. Water helps our letter flowers grow faster.

M05.text: Perfect! You don't have to hurry a flower, but you can help it along.

M06.text: See the bud? When the flower is ready, you'll be able to harvest it.

M07.text: Now pick the bloom. You can use a simple selection or the hand controls if you have them.

M08.text: Lovely! You've collected a letter for your Letter Bank and a cut flower for your flower collection.

M09.text: The letter and the flower are separate keepsakes. You can spend the letter without losing the flower.

M10.text: Practice here as often as you like. Nothing from this practice garden costs your real supplies.

M11.text: Would you like another try? Gardens are very patient teachers.

M12.text: You've got it! Return to Hudson when you're ready, and we'll see you again anytime.

H10.text: You've grown a flower! Now let's visit Kit. She knows practically everything about seeds.

H11.text: Kit has a practice wallet for you. Try different seeds without spending your actual coins.

K01.text: Oh! A customer! Welcome to my seed shop! I'm Kit. Please mind the seedlings. They're very nosy.

K02.text: See those seed packets? Pick whichever one interests you. This is a practice visit, so experiment!

K03.text: Those are practice coins, not your real money. Go on, try something fancy!

K04.text: A fine choice! Every seed is a little promise waiting to happen.

K05.text: When you shop for real, basic seeds have prices, and five-packs give you more for your coins.

K06.text: Basic seeds are always available. Some special things take a little longer to return.

K07.text: Sold out for now, but don't worry. More are on their way!

K08.text: Want to try another seed? I promise the practice wallet won't complain.

K09.text: Lovely doing business with you! Tell Hudson I sent you back with all your pockets intact.

H12.text: Next is Phineas, our carpenter. He'll show you the cart and how useful a crafted word can be.

P01.text: Hello there. I'm Phineas. I make things, mend things, and sometimes discover where I put my pencil.

P02.text: In Letter Town, a good word can become something useful. Letters are materials, and spelling is your craft.

P03.text: When you successfully craft a word, that crafted item goes into your Word Inventory. The letters you used are spent.

P04.text: Here's the cart. Select it to open a larger display where you can see what you're stocking. No need to poke at tiny shelves.

P05.text: The Word Cart holds crafted goods. The Flower Cart handles bouquets. They serve different purposes, so mind which one you're using.

P06.text: One day you'll have a home to furnish. Come see me when you're ready for furniture and other household work.

P07.text: That's enough tools for today. Hudson will guide you through an order next.

H13.text: Time to put all that practice together! We'll complete two little orders: first FLOWER, then MILK.

H14.text: Our first practice customer needs FLOWER. Gather or use the practice letters, then spell F-L-O-W-E-R.

H15.text: Need more letters? Go back to the practice garden. You can repeat without spending your real resources.

H16.text: That's FLOWER! You've crafted the item. Now hand it straight to the practice customer.

H17.text: Perfect delivery! This one goes directly to the customer, not onto the sales cart.

H18.text: Second order: MILK. Gather what you need, spell M-I-L-K, and craft the item.

H19.text: Excellent! This time, we'll stock the finished MILK in the Word Cart.

H20.text: Open the Word Cart, choose MILK from your practice Word Inventory, then select Stock.

H21.text: There it goes! Your customer bought the stocked MILK. You did it!

H22.text: FLOWER delivered and MILK sold! Your book has a completion stamp to remember the lesson.

H23.text: There's no hurry. Repeat anything you like, then return to me when you're ready to meet Mayor Ren.

H24.text: You've learned the basics! Time to meet Mayor Ren. He has something important to show you.

R01.text: Ah, our newest resident! Mayor Ren, at your service. What an extraordinary pleasure to welcome you to Letter Town.

R02.text: Snowy has already shown you the town map, I trust. Excellent. We'll use it to get you settled without another lecture.

R03.text: First, your garden: eight plots of your very own. Four are already growing, and four are ready for whatever you choose to plant.

R04.text: And to help you begin, you'll have your starting Letter Bank and one hundred coins.

R05.text: Next, a home! You'll choose from three cottage exteriors. The interior is modest, but it's yours to make extraordinary.

R06.text: Take a look at the three cottages. Choose the exterior that feels like home to you.

R07.text: Inside you'll find one large room and a smaller adjoining room. Both begin empty. Think of it as a blank page.

R08.text: Naturally, a mayor cannot welcome a neighbor empty-handed. Please choose one of these three housewarming gifts.

R09.text: A delightful choice! You may place it now or keep it safely in Home Storage until you're ready.

R10.text: Craft a useful word, trade for furnishings, or visit our talented residents. In time, you'll put your own stamp on every room.

R11.text: There is, however, one small matter. Our town's welcome sign could use some attention.

R12.text: When you're ready, help restore the welcome sign. It's a fine first project for a new neighbor.

R13.text: You may now browse the town improvement board. It shows projects and the materials they require.

R14.text: Craft the words and gather the materials the project calls for. Keep them in your inventory until you choose to contribute.

R15.text: Everything we need is here. Shall we restore our welcome sign?

R16.text: Splendid! Letter Town's welcome sign shines again. You have given our village a wonderful beginning.

R17.text: Friends and neighbors, a little celebration is in order! Here's to fresh letters, new flowers, and our newest resident.

R18.text: Our welcome sign is restored, but there's much more to enjoy. Your home, your garden, your neighbors—Letter Town is yours to explore.

H25.text: If you're wondering what to do next, the welcome sign is a good place to begin. Or explore a little first!

H26.text: Welcome back! Where would you like to begin: Home, Garden, or Town Square?

H27.text: While you were away, your cart may have made some sales. Check the cart for the latest update.

S10.text: Everything important is in your town book. Open the map tab to find your next stop.

S11.text: Need the instructions again? You can replay a conversation or review the lesson in your book.

S12.text: Your notes are up to date. The town is becoming easier to navigate already.

M13.text: This plot is empty and ready for a seed.

M14.text: Not quite ready yet. Watering can help it along, but it will keep growing while you're away.

M15.text: A lovely bloom! Your letter goes to the Letter Bank, and the cut flower goes to your flower collection.

M16.text: That was this plant's fifth harvest. The plot is free for a new seed!

K10.text: Welcome back! Looking for the everyday seeds, or something a little special?

K11.text: I can offer coins, or perhaps a trade. Let's see what you've got!

K12.text: All yours! I've placed it in your inventory.

K13.text: Not enough coins for that one just yet. Your other choices will still be here.

K14.text: A special trade! Here's a little package for you. Just select it to open.

K15.text: Would you like to keep shopping, or are you ready to check out?

P08.text: Back for a little building? Let's see what we can make.

P09.text: Choose an available spot for your item. You can move it or put it back in inventory whenever you like.

P10.text: Windows belong in the marked wall spots. Curtains attach separately, so you can change them later.

P11.text: For now, one wall finish and one flooring style per room. More precise decorating comes later.

P12.text: Choose a finished item, then Stock. Only goods you deliberately place on a cart can be sold.

P13.text: Looks like the cart is empty. Stock it when you're ready; no need to rush.

R19.text: Our town noticeboard has announcements, neighborly requests, and special trade offers. A useful little institution.

R20.text: You may help a resident, trade something they've requested, or simply continue your day. Good neighbors have choices.

R21.text: The welcome sign will wait until you're ready. A proper restoration deserves care, not hurry.

R22.text: The plaza is looking splendid. I suspect this is only the beginning of our town's story.

H28.text: To press a button, point at it with one finger, then pinch and let go. You can also tap it with a fingertip.

H29.text: Take your time. Nothing happens until you let go of the pinch, so you can aim first.

M17.text: To pick a flower, pinch it and pull gently. You can also poke the board in front of you and choose Pick.

P14.text: Until you've crafted something, flower arranging makes good practice. Pick up to nine flowers and keep the bouquet with you, or set it on the Flower Cart.

X01.text: A neighbor has a little story to share. Look for it at the noticeboard.
